definition_zh: 物主；所有者；产权人；业主
definition_en: a person who owns something, especially the person with the legal title to property or the head of a business
core_image: 门牌上写着名字，钥匙恰好插进那把锁
scene: 老巷尽头那家旧书店换了新主人。The new owner repainted the shop front in dark green.
sceneCN: 这里 owner 是「物主、所有者」（第 1 个义项：拥有某物的人）；句意为新店主把店面刷成了深绿色。图中可辨识物件：旧书店门脸、油漆桶、刷子。

derivatives.zh: 由 owner 加 -ship 构成，指所有权、产权
由 owner 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，指无主的
由 owner 与 occupied 复合而成，指由房主自住的

senses.title: A person who owns something
senses.definition: a person who has something as property, whether a house, a car or a pet
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为财产持有的人，可以是房子、汽车或宠物
senses.example: The owner of the little dog waited by the gate every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 那只小狗的主人每天傍晚都在门口等。
senses.why: Owner is own plus -er, the suffix that turns an action into a person, so the word names whoever holds the property.
senses.whyCN: owner 是 own 加 -er，这个后缀把动作变成人，所以这个词指持有那件财产的人。

senses.title: The person with the legal title
senses.definition: the person or company recorded in law as holding title to a property
senses.definitionCN: 在法律记录上持有某项财产所有权的人或公司
senses.example: The land owner refused to sell to the developer.
senses.exampleCN: 那位土地产权人拒绝把地卖给开发商。
senses.why: Because the verb own covers legal possession, adding -er produces the party a deed or register points to when ownership is disputed.
senses.whyCN: 既然动词 own 涵盖法律上的持有，加上 -er 就造出契据或登记簿在产权争议中指认的那一方。

senses.title: The head of a business
senses.definition: the person who runs and profits from a shop, company or sports club
senses.definitionCN: 经营一家店铺、公司或体育俱乐部并从中获利的人
senses.example: The new owner repainted the shop front in dark green.
senses.exampleCN: 新店主把店面的门脸重新刷成了深绿色。
senses.why: A business is treated as a thing that can be owned, so the same suffix names the person at the top of it, from a corner shop to a football club.
senses.whyCN: 生意被看作可以拥有的一样东西，于是同一个后缀也用来指站在它顶端的人，从街角小店到足球俱乐部都适用。

intro.en: Owner is an English formation from own and the suffix -er; no Latin ancestor is involved, and the word appears in Middle English.
intro.cn: owner 由 own 加后缀 -er 构成的英语词，不涉及拉丁语祖先，中古英语时期已经出现。

items.en: The base is āgan, to have and to hold, with its participle āgen meaning belonging to someone.
items.cn: 词基是 āgan，意为持有、拥有，其分词 āgen 意为「属于某人的」。

items.en: Middle English ownen, to possess, supplied the stem, and the agent suffix -er was added to name the person.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ownen（拥有）提供了词干，再加上表示行为者的后缀 -er 用来指人。

items.en: Forms such as ownere appear in records of land and goods, where a named person had to answer for what was held.
items.cn: ownere 这类形式出现在土地与货物的记录里，那里需要一个具名的人为所持之物负责。

items.en: With industry and property law, owner spread to shops, ships and companies, and compounds such as landowner became common.
items.cn: 随着工业与财产法的发展，owner 扩展到店铺、船只和公司，landowner 之类的复合词也变得常见。

items.en: Modern English uses owner for people and ownership for the abstract right, keeping the two endings clearly apart.
items.cn: 现代英语用 owner 指人，用 ownership 指抽象的权利，两个后缀分工清楚。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the base word and the suffixes that rebuild it; the near-meaning group gathers other names for the person who holds property.
note.cn: 形近组沿基础词和重建它的后缀展开；近义组收其他指「持有财产之人」的说法。

entries.definition: To have something as property, or belonging to oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物，或指属于自己的。

entries.definition: The legal right or state of owning something.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物的法定权利或状态。

entries.definition: A person who owns land.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有土地的人。

entries.definition: The owner of a business or property.
entries.definitionCN: 企业或房产的所有者。

entries.definition: A person who has something in their possession.
entries.definitionCN: 占有某物的人。

entries.definition: A person who owns a house or land and rents it out.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有房屋或土地并出租的人。

normalIntro.en: The word adds one suffix to a verb of holding, and everything else in the family simply adds another suffix to that person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词只是给表示持有的动词加了一个后缀，词族里其余的词又在这个「人」上继续加后缀。

normal.en: Owner is own plus -er: the suffix does nothing but turn holding into a person.
normal.cn: owner 是 own 加 -er：这个后缀只做一件事，把持有变成人。

normal.en: Ownership adds -ship to owner and turns the person back into an abstract right.
normal.cn: ownership 在 owner 后加 -ship，又把人变回一种抽象权利。

normal.en: Landowner and homeowner simply put the kind of property in front of the person.
normal.cn: landowner 与 homeowner 只是把财产种类放在人前面。

normal.en: The owner of a shop and the owner of a dog share one word because both answer for something.
normal.cn: 店主和狗主人共用一个词，因为两者都要为某样东西负责。

normal.en: Owe, own and owner all come from the same Old English verb of holding.
normal.cn: owe、own 与 owner 都来自同一个表示持有的古英语动词。

abstract.en: A person's name on a deed is a way of making a claim visible to everyone else.
abstract.cn: 地契上写下一个人的名字，是把一份主张变得人人可见的方法。

abstract.en: Ownership can be sold, lent or fought over, while the owner may change many times.
abstract.cn: 所有权可以被出售、出借或争夺，而所有者可能换了许多次。

abstract.en: Every owner is also someone who answers for what happens to the thing owned.
abstract.cn: 每个所有者同时也是那个要为所拥有之物的遭遇负责的人。

examples.en: The owner of the little dog waited by the gate every evening.
examples.cn: 那只小狗的主人每天傍晚都在门口等。

examples.en: The land owner refused to sell to the developer.
examples.cn: 那位土地产权人拒绝把地卖给开发商。

examples.en: The new owner repainted the shop front in dark green.
examples.cn: 新店主把店面的门脸重新刷成了深绿色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧呢」——问这东西是谁的，回答一声「欧呢」，就是主人；记住 owner 是所有者。

root: own（拥有）加 -er（表示人）构成；own 来自古英语 āgan（持有），与 owe 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the person behind a piece of property; the senses narrow into the legal title holder and widen again to the head of a business.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是财产背后那个人；义项一面收窄到法定产权人，一面又扩展到企业的老板。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name on a doorplate, and the one key that turns in the lock below it.
core.cn: 核心意象：门牌上写着名字，门下的锁只认那一把钥匙。

branches.en: a dog waiting by a gate for its person
branches.cn: 一条狗在门口等它的主人

branches.en: a deed with one name written on it
branches.cn: 写着一个人名字的地契

branches.en: a shopkeeper unlocking the door at dawn
branches.cn: 店主在清晨开门

branches.en: a club owner watching from the stands
branches.cn: 俱乐部老板在看台上观战

branches.en: a key turning in a lock that belongs to one name
branches.cn: 钥匙转动，锁只属于一个名字

intro.en: The word is a verb of holding plus the English person suffix -er, and the rest of the family adds suffixes to that person.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示持有的动词加上英语中表示人的后缀 -er，词族其余部分再在这个「人」上继续加后缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; it is an English noun built on a native verb plus -er.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它是由本土动词加 -er 构成的英语名词。

items.meaningCN: 做某事或持有某物的人

definition_zh: 所有权；拥有；归属关系
definition_en: the state or legal right of possessing something, or the relation by which a thing belongs to a person
core_image: 一枚刻着名字的铜牌钉在门上，钥匙挂在旁边，名字在牌上的人就有权处置屋内之物
scene: 产权登记处把房屋过户到买方名下，登记簿上的名字一换，处置权随之转移。The land registry transferred the house to the buyer, and once the name on the register changed, ownership passed with it.
sceneCN: 这里指「对某物享有法律上的所有权」，对应第 1 个义项：可以占有、使用与处置的权利；句意为登记簿上的名字一换，所有权随之转移。画面要点：门上的铜牌、挂着的钥匙、登记簿；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 所有权；拥有（不可数，常后接表示所属物的介词短语，指明所拥有之物）

derivatives.zh: 所有者；物主（动词加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
共有人（表示「共同」的前缀与所有者一词复合，指与他人共享所有权的人）
共有；共同所有（表示「共同」的前缀与所有权一词复合，指所有权由多人分享）
拥有；承认（古英语动词，指对某物有支配权，后引申为「承认某事属于自己」）

senses.title: The legal right to dispose of a thing
senses.titleCN: 对物进行处置的法律权利
senses.definition: the legal power to use, sell, give away or exclude others from a thing
senses.definitionCN: 使用、出售、赠予某物并排除他人使用的法律权力
senses.example: The land registry transferred the house to the buyer, and once the name on the register changed, ownership passed with it.
senses.exampleCN: 产权登记处把房屋过户给买方，登记簿上的名字一换，所有权随之转移。
senses.why: The word joins the verb 'to have' to a suffix for a condition, so it names a state of having that the law will protect.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表示「拥有」的动词与表状态的后缀结合，命名一种法律会保护的有有状态。

senses.title: Holding something in fact
senses.definition: the actual possession of a thing, whether or not the law recognises a title
senses.definitionCN: 实际持有某物，无论法律是否承认其权属
senses.example: Ownership of the keys does not always mean ownership of the flat.
senses.exampleCN: 拿着钥匙并不总意味着拥有这套公寓。
senses.why: Possession and title can come apart, and the word sometimes describes the plain fact of having rather than the right to have.
senses.whyCN: 占有与权属可以分开，这个词有时描述「手上确实有」这一事实，而不是「有权拥有」。

senses.title: The relation of belonging
senses.definition: the link by which a thing is attributed to a person, so that it answers to that person's name
senses.definitionCN: 某物被归到某人名下、对其名字作出回应的那种联系
senses.example: Ownership of the manuscript is disputed between two libraries.
senses.exampleCN: 这份手稿的归属在两家图书馆之间存有争议。
senses.why: Beyond the right and the fact lies a relation: the thing belongs to someone, and that belonging is what the noun most abstractly names.
senses.whyCN: 在权利与事实之外还有一层关系：物属于某人，而这种归属正是这个名词最抽象地命名的东西。

senses.title: Shareholding and proprietorship
senses.definition: the holding of shares in a company, or the position of a person who owns a firm
senses.definitionCN: 持有公司股份，或拥有某企业的业主地位
senses.example: Foreign ownership of the airline was capped at a fixed share.
senses.exampleCN: 该航空公司的外资持股被限定在固定比例内。
senses.why: When firms replace land as the main object of wealth, the same noun measures who holds the shares.
senses.whyCN: 当企业取代土地成为财富的主要对象，同一个名词就用来衡量谁持有股份。

senses.title: Public versus private regimes
senses.titleCN: 公有与私有的制度之分
senses.definition: the system under which the means of production or a service is held by the state or by private persons
senses.definitionCN: 生产资料或某项服务由国家持有还是由私人持有的制度安排
senses.example: The dispute was about ownership of the water supply, not about its price.
senses.exampleCN: 争论在于供水归谁所有，而不在于水价。
senses.why: Ownership becomes a political question once whole industries rather than single objects are at stake.
senses.whyCN: 一旦涉及的是整个行业而不是单件物品，所有权就成了政治问题。

senses.title: Personal responsibility for a task
senses.definition: the attitude of treating a problem or project as one's own, with the duty to see it through
senses.definitionCN: 把某个问题或项目当作自己的事、并承担完成责任的态度
senses.example: The team asked each member to take ownership of one part of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 团队要求每位成员对计划的一部分负起责任。
senses.why: Modern management borrowed the legal word and stripped the title from it, leaving only the sense of treating the work as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 现代管理借用了这个法律词，抽去了权属，只留下「把工作当作自己的事」这一层。

senses.title: Attribution of a work to its author
senses.definition: the legal and moral link between a creative work and the person who made it
senses.definitionCN: 创造性作品与其创作者之间的法律与道义联系
senses.example: Ownership of the copyright passed to the publisher for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 著作权中的财产权在十年内转给了出版方。
senses.why: A text or a design can belong to someone too, so the noun extends from goods to works of the mind.
senses.whyCN: 文本或设计同样可以属于某人，因此这个名词从货物延伸到心智作品。

senses.title: Tenure of land in older law
senses.definition: the holding of land under a lord or a superior, with duties attached, rather than outright title
senses.definitionCN: 在领主或上级之下持有土地并附带义务，而不是绝对的所有权
senses.example: In that period ownership of land carried service as well as rent.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个时期，土地保有权既带来地租，也带来服役义务。
senses.why: Before absolute title was common, holding land meant holding it of someone, and the word recorded that layered relation.
senses.whyCN: 在绝对所有权普及之前，持有土地意味着从某人那里持有，这个词记录了那种分层的关系。

intro.en: Ownership joins the Old English verb agan 'to have, possess' to the suffix -ship, which came from a word for shape or condition. Both parts are Germanic, and the compound is a native English formation rather than a borrowing.
intro.cn: ownership 由古英语动词 agan「拥有、占有」加后缀 -ship 构成，而后缀出自一个表示「形状、状态」的词。两部分都属日耳曼语，这个复合词是英语本族造词，而不是借词。

items.en: Agan 'to have, to possess' is the verb behind own, and it is Germanic, with recorded relatives in other old Germanic languages.
items.cn: agan 意为「有、占有」，是 own 背后的动词，属日耳曼语，在其他古老日耳曼语言中有可考的同族词。

items.en: The reconstructed verb is posited with a star; the deeper Indo-European root is also a reconstruction, so the earliest layer is not directly attested.
items.cn: 重构的动词形式以带星号的方式拟出；更深的印欧语词根同样属重构，因此最早的层次没有直接文献实证。

items.en: The suffix came from a word meaning 'shape, condition', and it built nouns for states, offices and skills.
items.cn: 这个后缀出自一个表示「形状、状态」的词，用来构成表示状态、职位与技艺的名词。

items.en: The compound joined the two and named the condition of one who has something, at first in ordinary rather than legal language.
items.cn: 这个复合词把两者结合，命名「拥有某物者的状态」，最初用于日常语言而非法律语言。

items.en: Lawyers later separated ownership from mere holding, giving the noun a technical sense that possession alone does not fill.
items.cn: 法学家后来把所有权与单纯的占有分开，使这个名词获得一个单靠占有无法填补的专业含义。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word also came to mean personal responsibility for a task. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，这个词也开始指对任务负起个人责任。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group is built from the same verb or looks close to it; the second group gives near alternatives from law, accounting and plain possession.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个动词构成或与它形近；第二组是来自法律、会计与日常占有三个方向的近义替代。

entries.definition: To possess, or belonging to oneself, as in one's own; it is the source word, while the entry noun names the relation.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有，或属于自己，如「自己的」；它是来源词，而本名词命名那种关系。

entries.definition: The person who holds title to a thing; the suffix marks a person, so the word cannot name the relation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物持有权属的人；后缀标示人，因此这个词不能命名关系本身。

entries.definition: Still to be paid, as in an owing sum; it comes from the verb owe, which is a different word from own.
entries.definitionCN: 尚待支付的，如「欠款」；它出自动词「欠」，与「拥有」是不同的词。

entries.definition: A person who owns the home he lives in; it joins the owner word to a word for occupying.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有并居住在自己房屋的人；它把「所有者」与「占用」两个词连在一起。

entries.definition: The fact of having something under one's control; it can exist without legal title, which is why the two are distinguished.
entries.definitionCN: 某物处于控制之下的事实；它可以没有法律权属而存在，因此两者被区分开。

entries.definition: The status of an owner, especially of a business; it is close in meaning but more formal and more often used of firms.
entries.definitionCN: 所有人的身份，尤指企业所有人；它意思相近，但更正式，也更常用于企业。

entries.definition: The legal right to own property, or the document proving it; it is the lawyer's word for the proof rather than the relation.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有财产的合法权利，或证明它的文件；它是法学家用来指证明而非关系的词。

entries.definition: The care and control of a person or thing, often without ownership; a custodian may hold what belongs to another.
entries.definitionCN: 对人或在物的照管与控制，往往不含所有权；保管人可以持有属于他人之物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Old English verb for having, the native suffix for a condition, real derived words and real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：古英语中表示「有」的动词、本族语中表状态的后缀、真实派生词与真实法律用语。

normal.en: The core is a name on a door: the thing answers to that name.
normal.cn: 核心是门上刻着的一个名字：那件东西对那个名字作出回应。

normal.en: The family runs own, owner, owners and co-ownership.
normal.cn: 同族词包括拥有、所有者、各位所有者与共有。

normal.en: Law separates the right from the holding, which is why possession alone is not ownership.
normal.cn: 法律把权利与占有分开，所以单有占有并不构成所有权。

normal.en: A company can be owned as surely as a field, so the word measures shares as well as soil.
normal.cn: 公司可以像田地一样被拥有，因此这个词既衡量股份，也衡量土地。

normal.en: Modern managers ask staff to take ownership of a problem, which keeps only the sense of treating it as one's own.
normal.cn: 现代管理者要求员工对问题「负起责任」，这里只保留了「把它当作自己的事」这一层。

abstract.en: Picture a brass plate on a door with a name cut into it, and a key hanging from the same hook.
abstract.cn: 想象门上钉着一块刻了名字的铜牌，同一只钩子上挂着钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture a register whose page is rewritten, and the right to the house moving with the ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一本登记簿的页面被改写，房屋的权利随墨迹一起转移。

abstract.en: Picture a worker who writes his own name on a task that no one assigned to him.
abstract.cn: 想象一名工人把名字写在一件没有人指派给他的任务上。

examples.en: Ownership of the building was split between two families.
examples.cn: 这栋楼的所有权由两户人家分有。

examples.en: The report recommends wider home ownership among younger households.
examples.cn: 报告建议让更多年轻家庭拥有自有住房。

examples.en: She took ownership of the delay and explained what went wrong.
examples.cn: 她承担了延误的责任，并解释了出错之处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧呢事普」——「欧」听成「我」，「呢」听成「的」：写着我的名字的那件东西，就是所有权。

root: 古英语 agan「拥有、占有」+ 古英语 -scipe「形状、状态」→ ownership。两部分均属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；该动词的日耳曼语祖形与更深的印欧语词根都属重构形式，无直接文献实证。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings start from a name on a door. The legal right to dispose comes first, then the plain fact of holding, then belonging as a relation; from there the word measures shares, divides public from private regimes, lends itself to personal responsibility, extends to works of the mind, and remembers an older layered tenure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从门上刻着的名字开始。先是对物处置的法律权利，其次是持有的事实，再其次是归属这一关系；由此这个词衡量股份、区分公有与私有、借给个人责任感、延伸到心智作品，并记得一种较早的分层保有权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name on a plate beside a key, marking who may dispose of what is behind the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙旁铜牌上的名字，标明谁有权处置门后之物。

branches.en: RIGHT AND HOLDING: the legal power to dispose, and the bare fact of having something in hand.
branches.cn: 权利与持有：处置的法律权力，以及手中确实有某物的事实。

branches.en: BELONGING: the relation that ties a thing to a name, including the older layered tenure of land.
branches.cn: 归属：把物与名字系在一起的关系，包括较早的分层土地保有权。

branches.en: SHARES: ownership measured in stock, and the position of a firm's proprietor.
branches.cn: 股份：以股票衡量的所有权，以及企业业主的地位。

branches.en: REGIMES: the political division between public and private holding.
branches.cn: 制度：公有与私有之间的政治分野。

branches.en: RESPONSIBILITY AND AUTHORSHIP: treating a task as one's own, and attributing a work to its maker.
branches.cn: 责任与作者身份：把任务当作自己的事，以及把作品归到创作者名下。

intro.en: This family is entirely Germanic: a verb for having plus a native suffix for a condition, with compounds built by adding person and place words.
intro.cn: 这个家族完全是日耳曼语的：一个表示「拥有」的动词，加上一个本族语的表状态后缀，再由表示人与处所的词构成复合形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this family. Latin-based near synonyms such as possession and proprietorship come from different roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个家族没有拉丁语来源。由拉丁语派生的近义词如「占有」与「所有权」出自不同的词根。

items.meaning: the condition of holding something as one's own
items.meaningCN: 把某物作为自己之物持有的状态
items.example: Ownership passed to the buyer on signature.
items.exampleCN: 签署之时所有权转移给买方。

items.example: They own the land beside the river.
The owners met to divide the rent.
items.exampleCN: 各位业主开会分配租金。

items.meaning: a holder of title shared with another
items.example: Each co-owner may use the whole garden.
items.exampleCN: 每位共有人都可以使用整个花园。

items.meaning: title shared by more than one person
items.exampleCN: 共有要求就修缮达成一致。

items.example: The landowner leased the field for ten years.
items.exampleCN: 地主把这块田租了十年。

items.meaning: a person who owns the house he lives in
items.example: Homeowners pay a local property tax.
items.exampleCN: 房主需缴纳地方房产税。

derivatives.zh: 所有者；物主（动词加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
共有人（表示「共同」的前缀与所有者一词复合，指与他人共享所有权的人）
共有；共同所有（表示「共同」的前缀与所有权一词复合，指所有权由多人分享）
拥有；承认（古英语动词，指对某物有支配权，后引申为「承认某事属于自己」）

definition_zh: 步速；速度；节奏；进度；踱步
definition_en: the speed at which a person or an animal moves, the rate at which an activity develops, or the act of walking back and forth
core_image: 跑道上一个人的步子均匀落下，鞋底一次次压在同一条白线上
scene: 跑道边的教练握着一块秒表，眼睛盯着从弯道冲出来的选手。The runner held a steady pace over the final lap.
sceneCN: 这里的 pace 是「步速、速度」（第 1 个义项：移动的快慢）；句意为这名选手在最后一圈保持了稳定的速度。图中可辨识物件：秒表、弯道、白线。

derivatives.zh: 由 pace 加表示「做某事的人或物」的 -er 构成，义为「领跑者；定速器」
由 pace 与 maker 复合而成，义为「领跑者；心脏起搏器」
由 pace 与 setter 复合而成，义为「定步速的人；带头人」

senses.title: The speed at which someone moves
senses.definition: the speed at which a person or an animal walks, runs or otherwise moves
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物行走、奔跑或移动的快慢
senses.example: The runner held a steady pace over the final lap.
senses.exampleCN: 这名选手在最后一圈保持了稳定的速度。
senses.why: Pace began as the Latin word for a single step, so the noun first counted steps on the ground; only later did it come to mean how fast those steps follow one another.
senses.whyCN: pace 起初是拉丁语中表示「一步」的词，所以这个名词最早数的是地上的步子；至于「步子迈得多快」，是后来才长出来的意思。

senses.title: The rate at which something develops
senses.definition: the speed at which an activity, a process or a period of time moves forward
senses.definitionCN: 活动、过程或一段时间向前推进的快慢
senses.example: The pace of change in the industry has surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行业变化的速度让所有人都感到意外。
senses.why: Once the word measured how quickly feet cover ground, it could measure how quickly anything else moves, so trade, study and daily life all acquired a pace of their own.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能量出双脚走完一段路的快慢，它就能量出别的任何事物推进的快慢，于是贸易、学业与日常生活都有了自己的节奏。

senses.title: To walk back and forth
senses.definition: to walk with regular steps across a room or a small area, especially while waiting or worrying
senses.definitionCN: 在一个房间或一小片地方来回走动，尤指等待或焦虑时
senses.example: He paced the corridor while the interview went on.
senses.exampleCN: 面试进行时，他在走廊里来回踱步。
senses.why: Since a step is the unit that pace counts, the verb simply names the act of taking steps; with no destination in view, those steps turn into restless walking to and fro.
senses.whyCN: 既然「一步」是 pace 所计的单位，动词自然就指迈步这件事；当眼前没有目的地时，这些步子就变成了焦躁的来回走动。

intro.en: Pace comes from Latin passus, a step, which itself grew out of pandere, to stretch out; French passed the word to English in the Middle Ages, first as a step and later as a rate of movement.
intro.cn: pace 来自拉丁语 passus（一步），而 passus 又出自 pandere（伸开）；中世纪时法语把这个词传给英语，先指一步，后指移动的快慢。

items.en: Pandere meant to spread or stretch out, and a leg stretching forward across the ground is the picture behind the whole family.
items.cn: pandere 意为展开、伸开，一条腿向前跨过地面，正是这一族词背后的画面。

items.en: Passus named a step or a stride, and Roman surveyors also used it for a fixed measure of length counted in double steps.
items.cn: passus 指一步或一个跨步，罗马的测量者也用它作固定的长度单位，按双步计算。

items.en: Old French kept the noun as pas, a step, and built a verb meaning to step or to walk.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词保留为 pas（一步），并造出表示迈步、行走的动词。

items.en: English borrowed pace in the thirteenth century for a step and for the length of a step, and the sense of speed followed from timing those steps.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 pace，指一步以及一步的长度；等到人们开始给这些步子计时，速度义就跟着出现了。

items.en: Modern English uses pace for walking speed, for the rhythm of any activity, and as a verb for walking to and fro.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pace 指步速、任何活动的节奏，也用作动词表示来回走动。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin step or on the English word itself; the near-meaning group collects words for speed and rhythm.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「步」之上或由这个词本身构成的词；近义组收表示速度与节奏的词。

normalIntro.en: Pace keeps the picture of a single step on the ground, and every later meaning is that step repeated at a certain rate.
normalIntro.cn: pace 始终保留「地上落下的一步」这个画面，后来的一切含义都是这一步以某种快慢重复下去。

normal.en: Pace goes back to Latin passus, a step, so the word began as something you could count on the ground.
normal.cn: pace 上溯拉丁语 passus（一步），所以它最初是地上数得出来的东西。

normal.en: Keep pace with keeps that picture: two people taking steps at the same rate, so neither falls behind.
normal.cn: keep pace with 保留了这个画面：两个人以同样的快慢迈步，谁也不会落后。

normal.en: A pacemaker was first a person who set the speed for a runner, and the same word now names the device that sets the rhythm of a heart.
normal.cn: pacemaker 最初指为跑者定速的人，如今同一个词也指给心脏定节奏的装置。

normal.en: Speed and pace are close, but pace often suggests a rhythm held over time, while speed is simply how fast something goes.
normal.cn: speed 与 pace 意思很近，但 pace 常暗示一段时间里维持住的节奏，而 speed 只是单纯有多快。

normal.en: French pas still means a step, which is why the two words look so alike.
normal.cn: 法语 pas 至今仍指一步，这正是两个词看起来如此相似的原因。

abstract.en: A word that started as one footfall suggests that all speed is finally a matter of repeated steps, one after another.
abstract.cn: 一个从一声脚步开始的词说明：一切速度最终都不过是一步接一步的重复。

abstract.en: To keep pace is to agree to move at someone else's rhythm, which is why the phrase sounds like a relationship and not only a measurement.
abstract.cn: 跟上步伐就是同意按别人的节奏移动，所以这个说法听起来像一种关系，而不只是一次测量。

abstract.en: A man pacing a corridor is measuring time with his feet, since waiting has no clock but does have steps.
abstract.cn: 在走廊里踱步的人其实在用脚量时间，因为等待没有钟表，却有一步步的移动。

examples.en: The runner held a steady pace over the final lap.
examples.cn: 这名选手在最后一圈保持了稳定的速度。

examples.en: The pace of change in the industry has surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 这个行业变化的速度让所有人都感到意外。

examples.en: He paced the corridor while the interview went on.
examples.cn: 面试进行时，他在走廊里来回踱步。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是反复落下的一步；义项按「这些步子的快慢」「任何活动获得的节奏」「无处可去时的来回走动」分出。

branches.en: an office where the work keeps speeding up

branches.en: a corridor worn thin by waiting feet

branches.en: one word for a daily rhythm and for restless steps
branches.cn: 同一个词，既指日常节奏，也指不安的踱步

senses.title: Something wrapped for sending or selling
senses.definition: something wrapped in paper, plastic or a box so that it can be carried, sent or sold

senses.example: The clerk handed her a heavy package wrapped in brown paper.

senses.example: The government announced a package of measures to help small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 政府公布了一揽子帮助小企业的措施。
senses.why: If one wrapper can hold several objects, the same noun can hold several proposals under one agreement, which is how the word reached politics, tourism and software.
senses.whyCN: 既然一层包装能装下好几样东西，同一个名词就能把好几项提议装进一份协议里，这个词就是这样走进了政治、旅游与软件。

senses.exampleCN: 他们把饼干装进小小的锡纸袋里。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: instead of naming the thing already packed, it names the act of packing it, and modern marketing stretched it to designing the wrapper as well.

intro.en: Package is an English formation of the sixteenth century, made from the old noun pack and the French ending -age; the root pack is usually traced to Middle Dutch or Middle Low German, so the word is Germanic rather than Latin.
intro.cn: package 是十六世纪英语自造的派生词，由古老名词 pack 与法语词尾 -age 构成；词根 pack 一般认为来自中古荷兰语或中古低地德语，因此这族词属日耳曼语而非拉丁语。

items.en: The noun pak meant a bundle tied up for carrying, and it is the usual source given for the English word pack.
items.cn: 名词 pak 指捆好便于搬运的包裹，通常被认为是英语 pack 的来源。

items.en: English took the noun as pack, a bundle or a load, and used it for goods tied together for a journey or a market.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词收作 pack，意为捆、一捆货，用来指为出行或赶集而捆在一起的货物。

items.en: The ending -age came into English through French from Latin -aticum and named an action or its result, as in voyage and baggage.
items.cn: 词尾 -age 经法语从拉丁语 -aticum 进入英语，表示动作或其结果，如 voyage 与 baggage。

items.en: Package first named both the act of packing and the bundle that resulted, and it soon covered goods prepared for a customer.
items.cn: package 最早同时指打包这个动作和打好的包，不久便用来指为顾客备好的货品。

items.en: Modern English adds package deal and package tour in trade and travel, the software package in computing, and the verb to package.
items.cn: 现代英语在商贸与旅游中加上 package deal 与 package tour，在计算机领域加上 software package，还发展出动词用法。

normal.cn: packet 是它的小兄弟：两个词都从 pack 长出来，但 packet 是纸或塑料的小容器，而 package 可以大到一个纸箱。

normal.en: Package deal borrows the parcel picture: several items tied together and sold as one.
normal.cn: package deal 借用了包裹的画面：几样东西捆在一起，当作一件来卖。

normal.en: The verb adds nothing except the act, so packaged goods are simply goods that have been put into their wrappers.
normal.cn: 动词只添上动作本身，所以 packaged goods 不过是已经装进包装的货物。

normal.en: British speakers often say parcel for something sent by post, while package is the usual word in American English.
normal.cn: 英式英语常用 parcel 指邮寄的东西，而美式英语里 package 才是通常的说法。

abstract.en: A word that means a tied bundle keeps reminding us that selling often consists of deciding what to tie together.
abstract.cn: 一个意为「捆好的包」的词反复提醒人：所谓销售，常常就是决定把什么捆在一起。

abstract.en: A package deal hides its seams: the wrapping makes several separate things look like one decision.
abstract.cn: 一揽子交易藏起了接缝：包装让几件彼此独立的事看起来像同一个决定。

abstract.en: Wrapping protects a thing and also hides it, which is why the same word can mean care and concealment.
abstract.cn: 包装既保护一件东西，也遮住这件东西，所以同一个词既能表示用心，也能表示遮掩。

examples.en: The clerk handed her a heavy package wrapped in brown paper.
examples.cn: 店员递给她一个用牛皮纸包好的沉包裹。

examples.en: The government announced a package of measures to help small firms.
examples.cn: 政府公布了一揽子帮助小企业的措施。

examples.en: The company spent millions on packaging that can be recycled.
examples.cn: 这家公司花了大笔钱用于可回收的包装。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派克吉」——派克把东西捆成一包再贴上标签；记住 package 是包裹、一揽子方案。

root: 由中古英语 pack（一捆，一般认为来自中古荷兰语或低地德语 pak）加法语词尾 -age（动作或结果）构成，十六世纪出现；词根属日耳曼语，无可靠的拉丁同族词，只有词尾 -age 经法语上溯拉丁语 -aticum。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bundle tied and sealed; the senses divide into the object itself, a set of things sold under one wrapping, and the act of wrapping them.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个捆好封好的包；义项按「包本身」「包在同一层包装里的一套东西」「把它们包起来的动作」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown paper parcel crossed by twine, the knot pressed flat in the middle.
core.cn: 核心意象：柜台上一只棕色纸包被麻绳十字捆紧，绳结压在正中间。

branches.en: a parcel pushed across a counter
branches.cn: 从柜台上推过来的一只包裹

branches.en: a carton sealed with tape before a van leaves
branches.cn: 货车出发前用胶带封好的纸箱

branches.en: a list of measures signed as one document
branches.cn: 作为一份文件签署的一组措施

branches.en: a holiday whose flight and hotel are sold together
branches.cn: 机票与旅馆合起来出售的一次度假

branches.en: hands folding foil around a row of biscuits
branches.cn: 双手把锡纸裹在一排饼干上

intro.en: The word is an old Germanic noun for a bundle wearing a French noun ending, so its parts still say a packed thing and the result of packing.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个意为「捆」的古老日耳曼名词，披着法语名词词尾，各部分至今仍在说「被捆好的东西」与「打包的结果」。

latinIntro.en: The root pack has no reliable Latin cognate; only the noun ending -age reached English through French from Latin -aticum, so no Latin word is listed for the root itself.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 pack 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；只有名词词尾 -age 经法语上溯拉丁语 -aticum，因此词根本身不列拉丁词。

definition_zh: 小包；小袋；数据包；一大笔钱
definition_en: a small container made of paper or plastic holding a measured amount of something, a unit of data sent across a network, or, in British informal use, a large sum of money
core_image: 柜台上一个透明小袋被撕开一角，几块饼干从里面露出半边
scene: 便利店的柜台上摆着一个透明的小袋，里面装着几颗糖果。He tore open a packet of biscuits and shared them out.
sceneCN: 这里的 packet 是「小包、小袋」（第 1 个义项：装少量物品的纸袋或塑料袋）；句意为他撕开一包饼干分给大家。图中可辨识物件：透明小袋、糖果、柜台。

pos.zh: 小包；小袋；数据包；一大笔钱

derivatives.zh: 由 packet（邮包）与 boat 复合而成，义为「定期邮船」
由 packet 与 switched 复合而成，义为「分组交换的」
由 packet 与 sniffer 复合而成，义为「数据包嗅探工具」

senses.title: A small paper or plastic container
senses.definition: a small container of paper, plastic or foil holding a measured amount of something such as biscuits, cigarettes or seeds
senses.definitionCN: 用纸、塑料或锡箔做成的小容器，装着一定量的饼干、香烟或种子等
senses.example: He tore open a packet of biscuits and shared them out.
senses.exampleCN: 他撕开一包饼干分给大家。
senses.why: Packet is a pack with a small ending on it: French -et marks something little, so the word means a little pack before it means anything else.
senses.whyCN: packet 是 pack 加上一个表示「小」的词尾：法语 -et 指小的东西，所以这个词最原始的意思就是「小包」。

senses.title: A unit of data sent across a network
senses.definition: a small unit into which a message is divided so that it can travel separately across a network
senses.definitionCN: 把信息切开后形成的小单元，使它能在网络中分别传输
senses.example: Each packet carries the address of its destination.
senses.exampleCN: 每个数据包都带着目的地的地址。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the word because a message is cut into small wrapped units, each addressed and sent alone, and the whole is rebuilt at the other end.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用这个词，是因为信息被切成一个个包好、写好地址、单独发送的小单元，到了另一端再重新拼起来。

senses.title: A large sum of money
senses.definition: a lot of money, used in British informal speech especially with the verbs cost and spend
senses.definitionCN: 很多钱，用于英式口语，常与 cost、spend 这类动词连用
senses.example: That new car must have cost a packet.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆新车一定花了一大笔钱。
senses.why: British slang stretched the little parcel in the opposite direction: what is small in size became heavy in price, so the modest packet turned into a serious amount of money.
senses.whyCN: 英式俚语把这个小包朝反方向拉：体积上小的东西变成价钱上重的，于是不起眼的一小包成了实打实的一大笔钱。

intro.en: Packet is a diminutive of pack, formed with the French ending -et; English has used it since the sixteenth century for a small parcel, for a mail boat, and in modern times for a unit of data.
intro.cn: packet 是 pack 的指小形式，由法语词尾 -et 构成；英语从十六世纪起用它指小包裹、邮政船，到了现代又用它指数据单元。

items.en: English pack meant a bundle tied up, a word usually traced to Middle Dutch or Middle Low German pak.
items.cn: 英语 pack 指捆好的一包，一般认为来自中古荷兰语或中古低地德语 pak。

items.en: The ending -et came through French, ultimately from a Latin diminutive, and it marks a smaller version of the base word.
items.cn: 词尾 -et 经法语传来，最终出自拉丁语的指小形式，用来标出比原词更小的东西。

items.en: Packet first meant a small parcel or a bundle of letters, and it was the ordinary word for a packet of papers.
items.cn: packet 最早指小包裹或一捆信件，当时是「一叠文件」的常用说法。

items.en: A packet boat was a ship that carried the mail packets, and the ship itself was soon shortened to packet.
items.cn: packet boat 指运送邮包的船，不久人们就干脆把这种船叫作 packet。

items.en: Modern English keeps the little container, adds the data packet of computing, and uses cost a packet for a very large price.
items.cn: 现代英语保留小容器义，加上计算机领域的数据包义，又用 cost a packet 表示价钱极高。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on pack plus a small ending, with one false friend included; the near-meaning group collects words for small containers of goods.
note.cn: 形近组收由 pack 加指小词尾构成的词，并收入一个假朋友；近义组收表示装少量物品的小容器的词。

entries.definition: A bundle of things, or to put them into a container.
entries.definitionCN: 一捆东西，或把东西装进容器。

entries.definition: A wrapped parcel of any size, or a set of things sold together.
entries.definitionCN: 任意大小的包裹，或合在一起出售的一套东西。

entries.definition: A person or machine that packs goods.
entries.definitionCN: 打包的人或机器。

entries.definition: A small bag sewn into clothing for carrying things; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 缝在衣服里装东西的小袋；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A small sealed bag holding a single portion of something.
entries.definitionCN: 装一份用量的密封小袋。

entries.definition: A small soft bag, often closed with a drawstring.
entries.definitionCN: 柔软的小袋，常用绳子收口。

entries.definition: A cardboard box or a sealed container for liquids.
entries.definitionCN: 纸板盒，或装液体的密封容器。

entries.definition: Something wrapped and tied, especially for post.
entries.definitionCN: 包好捆上的东西，尤指邮寄的包裹。

normalIntro.en: Packet is a pack shrunk by a French ending, so its hooks keep the picture of a small handful wrapped in paper or foil.
normalIntro.cn: packet 是被法语词尾缩小的 pack，记忆钩子保留「一小把东西裹在纸或锡箔里」的画面。

normal.en: Packet is pack plus the French diminutive -et, so the word says small pack in its very shape.
normal.cn: packet 是 pack 加法语指小词尾 -et，所以这个词的形状本身就在说「小包」。

normal.en: A packet is much smaller than a package: a packet fits in a pocket, while a package can need both arms.
normal.cn: packet 比 package 小得多：一包能塞进口袋，而一个包裹可能要双手才抱得住。

normal.en: Packet boat named a ship that carried the mail packets, and the ship later took the short name packet.
normal.cn: packet boat 指运送邮包的船，后来船本身也简称为 packet。

normal.en: British speakers say a packet of cigarettes where American speakers usually say a pack of cigarettes.
normal.cn: 英式英语说 a packet of cigarettes，而美式英语通常说 a pack of cigarettes。

normal.en: In computing the packet is wrapped, addressed and sent alone, which is why the postal picture transferred so easily.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，数据包被封装、写上地址、单独发送，所以邮政的画面能这么自然地搬过来。

abstract.en: A diminutive ending quietly tells us how much size matters in language: the same root can name a carton or a pocket-sized bag.
abstract.cn: 一个指小词尾悄悄说明尺寸在语言里多么重要：同一个词根既能指纸箱，也能指口袋大小的一包。

abstract.en: The same word holding a few biscuits and a unit of data suggests that a network is only a postal system made of light.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指几块饼干，也指一个数据单元，这说明网络不过是一个用光做的邮政系统。

abstract.en: Calling a huge bill a packet is a joke about size, and the joke works because the thing named is so small.
abstract.cn: 把巨额账单叫作一小包，是关于尺寸的玩笑，而这玩笑之所以成立，正因为被命名的东西如此之小。

examples.en: He tore open a packet of biscuits and shared them out.
examples.cn: 他撕开一包饼干分给大家。

examples.en: Each packet carries the address of its destination.
examples.cn: 每个数据包都带着目的地的地址。

examples.en: That new car must have cost a packet.
examples.cn: 那辆新车一定花了一大笔钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派克特」——派克特把一小把东西塞进纸袋，袋子只有巴掌大；记住 packet 是小包、小袋。

root: 由中古英语 pack（一捆，一般认为来自中古荷兰语或低地德语 pak）加法语指小词尾 -et 构成，十六世纪出现；与 package 同源，但 packet 指小容器，package 可指任意大小的包裹；词根属日耳曼语，无可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a little pack; the senses divide into the small container itself, the addressed units a network sends, and the slang use for a heavy price.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个小包；义项按「小容器本身」「网络发送的带地址单元」「俚语里的高额花费」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear little bag torn at one corner, biscuits showing through the opening.
core.cn: 核心意象：柜台上一个透明小袋被撕开一角，几块饼干从里面露出半边。

branches.en: a bag of sweets standing by the till
branches.cn: 收银台边立着的一袋糖

branches.en: a torn corner and crumbs on a counter
branches.cn: 撕开的一角与柜台上的碎屑

branches.en: a message cut into pieces that travel apart
branches.cn: 被切成若干块分别传输的一条信息

branches.en: a label on each piece naming where it should go
branches.cn: 每一块上标明去向的标签

branches.en: the same small word for a bag and for a big bill
branches.cn: 同一个不起眼的小词，既指小袋，也指大账单

intro.en: The word is a Germanic noun for a bundle with a French ending for small things, so its parts say plainly a little bundle.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个意为「捆」的日耳曼名词，加上法语中表示小东西的词尾，各部分明白地说出「一小捆」。

latinIntro.en: The root pack has no reliable Latin cognate; the small ending came through French and is only distantly Latin, so no Latin word is listed for this root.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 pack 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；指小词尾经法语传来，与拉丁语只有很远的关联，因此这一词根不列拉丁词。

definition_zh: 衬垫；护垫；便笺本；拍纸簿；填塞；轻步走
definition_en: a soft piece of material used for protection or comfort, a block of paper for writing, to stuff something with soft material, or to walk with soft quiet steps
core_image: 书桌一角压着一本被撕去几页的便笺本，纸页边缘参差不齐
scene: 书桌一角放着一本撕过几页的便笺本，旁边躺着一支笔。She wrote the address on a pad by the telephone.
sceneCN: 这里的 pad 是「便笺本」（第 2 个义项：一叠可撕的纸）；句意为她把地址写在电话旁的便笺本上。图中可辨识物件：便笺本、撕开的纸边、笔。

derivatives.zh: 由 pad 双写 d 加 -ing 构成，义为「填充物；赘语」
由 pad 双写 d 加 -ed 构成，义为「有衬垫的」
由 note 与 pad 复合而成，义为「便笺本」

senses.title: A soft piece used for protection or comfort
senses.definition: a piece of soft material placed under or against something to protect it, soften it or make it more comfortable
senses.definitionCN: 垫在某物下面或贴着某物的柔软材料，用来保护、缓冲或增加舒适
senses.example: The chair needs a new pad on the seat.
senses.exampleCN: 这把椅子的座面上需要一块新衬垫。
senses.why: Pad first named a soft bundle used as a bed or a cushion, so the word starts with something yielding placed under the body rather than with any shape.
senses.whyCN: pad 最初指当作床铺或坐垫的软捆，所以这个词的起点是垫在身体下面的一块软东西，而不是某个形状。

senses.title: A block of paper for writing
senses.definition: a number of sheets of paper glued together along one edge so that they can be torn off one by one
senses.definitionCN: 把若干张纸沿一边粘在一起，可以一张张撕下来使用
senses.example: She wrote the address on a pad by the telephone.
senses.exampleCN: 她把地址写在电话旁的便笺本上。
senses.why: A writing pad is a flat block of sheets, and that flat soft block looks exactly like the cushion the word already named, so one word covered both.
senses.whyCN: 便笺本是一叠压平的纸，而这个平整柔软的块状物，看起来正像这个词早先指的坐垫，于是一个词兼指两样东西。

senses.title: To stuff or line with soft material
senses.definition: to fill or cover something with soft material so that it is protected, fuller or more comfortable
senses.definitionCN: 用柔软材料把某物填满或包住，使它受到保护、更饱满或更舒适
senses.example: They padded the box with newspaper before posting it.
senses.exampleCN: 寄出之前，他们用报纸把箱子填塞好。
senses.why: The verb turns the cushion into an action: to pad something is to put a pad inside it, and from packing a box the sense spread to padding a speech with extra words.
senses.whyCN: 动词把坐垫变成动作：给某物加衬，就是往里面塞垫料；从给箱子填塞出发，这个意思又扩展到用多余的话把发言拉长。

senses.title: To walk quietly with soft steps
senses.definition: to walk with soft, quiet steps, especially with bare feet or paws
senses.definitionCN: 脚步轻软、几乎没有声响地走，尤指赤脚或动物用肉垫行走
senses.example: He padded across the room in bare feet.
senses.exampleCN: 他赤着脚轻轻走过房间。
senses.why: Bare feet or an animal's soft paw lands without a sound, and the word for a soft cushion became the verb for a walk that sounds like one.
senses.whyCN: 赤脚或动物的软掌落地几乎没有声响，于是「软垫」这个词又变成动词，指一种听上去像踩在垫子上的走法。

intro.en: The origin of pad is uncertain; the cushion sense is recorded in the sixteenth century, and one common suggestion links it to a Low German or Dutch word for the sole of the foot, but no origin is settled.
intro.cn: pad 的来源不确定；坐垫义在十六世纪已有记录，一种常见的推测把它联系到低地德语或荷兰语中表示脚掌的词，但没有定论。

items.en: The noun pad for a cushion appears in the sixteenth century, and dictionaries disagree about its source; a Low German or Dutch word for the sole of the foot is often suggested.
items.cn: 表示坐垫的名词 pad 在十六世纪出现，各词典对它的来源说法不一，常有人推测与低地德语或荷兰语中表示脚掌的词有关。

items.en: Pad named a soft bundle, a straw bed and a cushion, and it was also used for the stuffed saddle of a horse.
items.cn: pad 指软捆、草铺与坐垫，也曾用来指马背上加软垫的鞍。

items.en: The noun widened to any soft guard worn on the body, and the verb appeared with the sense of stuffing something with soft material.
items.cn: 词义扩展到身上穿的任何软护具，动词也随之出现，表示往某物里塞软材料。

items.en: A pad of paper named a block of sheets glued at one edge, and the verb gained the sense of walking with soft, quiet steps.
items.cn: a pad of paper 指沿一边粘住的一叠纸；动词也获得了脚步轻软地走这一义。

items.en: Modern English adds notepad, mouse pad and launch pad, keeps padding for stuffing material, and uses pad out for filling a text with needless matter.
items.cn: 现代英语加上 notepad、mouse pad 与 launch pad，保留 padding 表示填充物，也用 pad out 指用多余内容把文字拉长。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on pad or spelled close to it, including one false friend; the near-meaning group collects words for soft cushions, mats and paper blocks.
note.cn: 形近组收由 pad 构成或拼写相近的词，并收入一个假朋友；近义组收表示软垫、垫子与纸本的词。

entries.definition: Soft material used to fill or protect something, or needless words.
entries.definitionCN: 用来填充或保护的软材料，也指赘语。

entries.definition: Lined or filled with soft material.
entries.definitionCN: 加过衬垫或填过软材料的。

entries.definition: A small block of paper for taking notes.
entries.definitionCN: 用来记笔记的小本子。

entries.definition: A small metal lock with a hinged bar; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 带活动锁梁的小金属锁；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A soft bag of material used to sit or lean on.
entries.definitionCN: 坐或靠时用的软垫。

entries.definition: A flat piece of material laid on a floor or a table.
entries.definitionCN: 铺在地面或桌上的平垫。

entries.definition: A book of blank pages for writing notes.
entries.definitionCN: 供记笔记的空白本子。

entries.definition: A thick soft mass of material pressed together.
entries.definitionCN: 压在一起的一团软材料。

normalIntro.en: Pad is a short word for something soft and flat, and its hooks follow that flatness from a cushion to a block of paper and to a quiet footfall.
normalIntro.cn: pad 是一个表示「软而平的东西」的短词，记忆钩子顺着这份平整，从坐垫走到一叠纸，再走到一声轻软的脚步。

normal.en: Pad doubles its final consonant before a suffix, so the forms are padded and padding rather than paded.
normal.cn: pad 在加后缀前要双写末尾的辅音，所以形式是 padded 与 padding，而不是 paded。

normal.en: A pad of paper and a shoulder pad share one idea: a flat soft block that sits against something.
normal.cn: 一叠便笺纸与一块肩垫共有一个想法：一块平软的垫状物贴着别的东西。

normal.en: Padlock has nothing to do with a cushion, so the two words only look alike and must not be confused.
normal.cn: padlock 与坐垫毫无关系，两个词只是长得像，不能混为一谈。

normal.en: To pad a speech is to stuff it, exactly as a box is stuffed with paper before posting.
normal.cn: 给发言注水就是往里塞东西，和寄包裹前往箱子里塞纸一模一样。

normal.en: Pad across and pad along describe bare feet or soft paws, never the sound of heavy boots.
normal.cn: pad across 与 pad along 描写的都是赤脚或柔软的脚掌，绝不是沉重靴子的声响。

abstract.en: A word that means both a cushion and a notebook suggests that comfort and record-keeping can rest on the same flat softness.
abstract.cn: 一个词既指坐垫又指便笺本，说明舒适与记录可以建立在同一种平软之物上。

abstract.en: Padding protects a fragile thing and also makes it look bigger, which is why the same idea describes a parcel and a bloated essay.
abstract.cn: 填充既保护易碎之物，也让它显得更大，所以同一个概念既能说包裹，也能说一篇注水的文章。

abstract.en: Walking padded is walking as if the floor were a cushion, and the word quietly turns the ground into something kind.
abstract.cn: 轻步走就像把地板当成一块软垫，这个词悄悄把地面变成了温和的东西。

examples.en: The chair needs a new pad on the seat.
examples.cn: 这把椅子的座面上需要一块新衬垫。

examples.en: She wrote the address on a pad by the telephone.
examples.cn: 她把地址写在电话旁的便笺本上。

examples.en: He padded across the room in bare feet.
examples.cn: 他赤着脚轻轻走过房间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派德」——派德把一叠纸垫在桌上，写字时手肘不硌；记住 pad 是便笺本、衬垫。

root: 来源不确定，一般认为与低地德语或荷兰语中表示脚掌的词有关，也可能出自更早的日耳曼语；十六世纪已有记录，先指软垫、草铺，后指便笺本、填充与轻步走，无可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a flat soft block; the senses divide into the cushion itself, the paper block that looks like one, the act of stuffing, and the soft footfall that sounds like one.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一块平软的垫状物；义项按「坐垫本身」「形状相似的纸本」「塞入软物的动作」「听来像踩垫子的轻步」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small writing pad on a desk corner, its torn edges uneven.
core.cn: 核心意象：书桌一角压着一本被撕去几页的便笺本，纸页边缘参差不齐。

branches.en: a chair seat that has gone thin
branches.cn: 坐面已经磨薄的一把椅子

branches.en: a torn sheet beside a telephone
branches.cn: 电话旁被撕下的一页纸

branches.en: a block of sheets glued at one edge
branches.cn: 沿一边粘住的一叠纸

branches.en: newspaper crushed into the corners of a box
branches.cn: 被塞进箱角的报纸

branches.en: bare feet crossing a wooden floor
branches.cn: 赤脚走过木地板

intro.en: The word is short and its source is uncertain, so the parts that can be shown are its English compounds and the suffixes that make it a noun, an adjective and a verb.
intro.cn: 这个词很短，来源也不确定，所以能够指明的部分，是它的英语复合词，以及把它变成名词、形容词与动词的各个后缀。

latinIntro.en: The origin of pad is uncertain and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded, so no Latin word is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: pad 的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，因此这里不列拉丁词。

items.meaning: a soft cushion or a block of paper
to stuff or to walk softly
forming a noun of action or material
items.meaningCN: 后缀：构成动作或材料名词
后缀：构成表状态的形容词

items.meaning: soft material used to fill a space
a small pad of paper for notes
a mat for a computer mouse

definition_zh: 页；书页；网页；页面；呼叫；翻页
definition_en: one side of a sheet in a book or newspaper, a screen of content on a website, or to call out a name in a public place
core_image: 书页一角被风掀起，露出上一行还没读完的字
scene: 午后的阅览室里，风扇把摊开的书吹得轻轻翻动。He turned the page and found a note in the margin.
sceneCN: 这里 page 是「书页」（第 1 个义项：书本或报纸的一面）；句意是他翻过这一页，在页边空白处发现一行批注。图中可辨识的物件：摊开的书、风扇、页边批注。

collocations.zh: 翻过这一页；翻开新的一页
让人一页接一页读下去的

derivatives.zh: 由 page 加 -ing 构成，指广播或设备里的分页呼叫
由 page 加表示工具或人的后缀 -er 构成，指寻呼机
由拉丁 pagina（页）加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「给……编页码」
由 paginate 加 -ion 构成，义为「页码编排」

senses.title: One side of a sheet in a book or newspaper
senses.definition: one side of a single sheet of paper in a book, magazine or newspaper
senses.definitionCN: 书、杂志或报纸中一张纸的一面
senses.example: She dog-eared the page to mark her place.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那一页折了个角，标住自己读到哪儿。
senses.why: Latin pagina named the column of writing on a papyrus sheet, so the word began as the surface that carries text rather than the sheet itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pagina 本指纸草上书写的一栏文字，所以这个词最初指承载文字的那一面，而不是整张纸。

senses.title: A screen of content on a website
senses.definition: a single screen of content that a browser loads from a website
senses.definitionCN: 浏览器从网站载入的一屏内容
senses.example: The error page told us the link had expired.
senses.exampleCN: 那个错误页面提示我们链接已经失效。
senses.why: When text moved from paper to glass, the old word for a readable surface was simply carried over to what a browser shows.
senses.whyCN: 文字从纸面搬到玻璃屏上之后，人们就把这个表示「可读表面」的旧词直接搬去指浏览器显示的内容。

senses.title: To call a name out over a speaker
senses.definition: to call someone's name through a loudspeaker or an electronic device in order to reach them
senses.definitionCN: 通过扩音器或电子设备呼叫某人的名字，以便找到对方
senses.example: The airport staff paged her twice before she heard it.
senses.exampleCN: 机场工作人员呼叫了她两次，她才听见。
senses.why: This sense is usually said to come from the page who ran messages in a household; sending a name out to find a person survived after the servant vanished.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项一般认为来自旧时在宅院里跑腿传话的侍童；侍童消失了，但「把名字传出去找人」的做法留了下来。

senses.title: To look through a book page by page
senses.definition: to turn the pages of a book or magazine quickly while looking at them
senses.definitionCN: 快速翻动书或杂志的页面，一边翻一边看
senses.example: He paged through the atlas while waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 他等的时候一页页翻着那本地图册。
senses.why: The verb only turns the noun into an action: if a page is the unit of a book, then to page is to move through those units.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把名词变成动作：既然页是书的单位，那么翻页就是沿着这些单位一路往下走。

intro.en: Page goes back to a Latin noun for a column of writing, and English later used the same word for servants, web screens and loudspeaker calls.
intro.cn: page 可追到拉丁语中表示「书写的一栏」的名词，英语后来用同一个词指侍从、网页和广播呼叫。

items.en: Pagina meant a column of writing on a papyrus roll, and it is generally thought to come from the verb pangere.
items.cn: pagina 指纸草卷上的一栏文字，一般认为出自动词 pangere。

items.en: Pangere meant to fasten or plant, and the link to writing is usually explained as lines fixed onto a surface.
items.cn: pangere 意为固定、插下；它与书写的联系，一般认为是指一行行字被「固定」在表面上。

items.en: Old French page named both a leaf of a book and a young servant, and English took over both meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 page 既指书的一页，也指年轻的侍从，英语把这两个意思都接了过来。

items.en: Middle English page kept the book sense and the servant sense side by side for centuries.
items.cn: 中古英语的 page 让「书页」和「侍从」两个意思并行了好几百年。

items.en: Modern English added the newspaper page, the web page, and the verbs for calling a name and turning pages.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上报纸版面、网页，以及「呼叫名字」和「翻页」的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the Latin stem for a written column; the near-meaning group collects words for paper leaves and for calling someone.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在「书写的一栏」这一拉丁词干上的形式；近义组收表示纸页和呼唤某人的词。

entries.definition: The Latin noun for a column of writing, the source of the English word.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示书写栏目的名词，是英语这个词的来源。

entries.definition: To number the pages of a document.
entries.definitionCN: 给文件的各页编上页码。

entries.definition: A small device that beeps when someone is trying to reach you.
entries.definitionCN: 有人找你时会响的小型设备；寻呼机。

entries.definition: A public show with costumes and scenes; it is only close in spelling, and its source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 有服装和场景的公开演出；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A single piece of paper, or one side of it.
entries.definitionCN: 一张纸，或纸的一面。

entries.definition: A sheet of paper in a book, especially when numbered on both sides.
entries.definitionCN: 书中一张纸，尤指两面都编了号的。

entries.definition: What a device shows at one time.
entries.definitionCN: 设备一次显示的内容；屏幕。

entries.definition: To call someone to come, often officially.
entries.definitionCN: 召唤某人前来，常带正式意味。

normalIntro.en: Page began as the written surface of a roll, and its family keeps two ideas alive: numbered leaves and calling a name out.
normalIntro.cn: page 最初指卷轴上书写的那一面，同族词一直保有两个想法：编了号的纸页，以及把名字喊出去。

normal.en: Latin pagina is the written column, so page is first a surface that holds text.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pagina 是书写的一栏，所以 page 首先是承载文字的表面。

normal.en: Pangere means to fasten, which is why pagina is often explained as lines fixed onto a surface.
normal.cn: pangere 意为固定，所以一般认为 pagina 就是被固定在表面上的一行行字。

normal.en: The suffix -ate in paginate turns the noun into a verb: to give a document its page numbers.
normal.cn: paginate 里的后缀 -ate 把名词变成动词，意思是给文件编上页码。

normal.en: The servant sense survives in the verb to page someone, because a page carried messages by name.
normal.cn: 「侍从」这个意思留在动词 to page 里，因为侍从就是按名字替人传话的。

normal.en: Web page puts the old word on a new surface, so the meaning moves from paper to screen without changing its core.
normal.cn: 网页只是把这个旧词放到新的表面上，词义从纸移到屏幕，核心并没有变。

abstract.en: A page is a unit small enough to finish, which is why turning the page can mean starting over.
abstract.cn: 一页小到能读完，所以「翻过这一页」也可以表示重新开始。

abstract.en: Numbering pages makes a book addressable: any sentence can be found again later.
abstract.cn: 给页编号让整本书可以被定位：任何一句话以后都能重新找到。

abstract.en: One word covers paper, screens and loudspeaker calls because all three put a name or a text where someone can meet it.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖纸、屏幕和广播，因为这三者都是把名字或文字放到别人能遇上的地方。

examples.en: He turned the page and found a note in the margin.
examples.cn: 他翻过这一页，在页边发现一行批注。

examples.en: The site's help page explains how to reset the password.
examples.cn: 网站的帮助页面说明了如何重设密码。

examples.en: The nurse paged the doctor at midnight.
examples.cn: 护士在午夜呼叫了医生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佩奇」——翻开书页，小猪佩奇正坐在页码上；page 是书页，也是呼叫。

root: 拉丁语 pagina（书写的一栏）一般认为出自 pangere（固定、钉住），经古法语 page 进入英语；同族词多与纸页、编号有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a written surface you can turn; from it come the book page, the web page, the act of turning pages, and the call that sends a name out.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一面可以翻动的书写表面；书页、网页、翻页的动作，以及把名字喊出去的呼叫，都由此展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the corner of a page lifting in a breeze, showing the line above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：书页一角被风掀起，露出上一行还没读完的字。

branches.en: a reader folding a corner to keep the place
branches.cn: 读者折起页角记住读到哪儿

branches.en: a browser showing the same old word on glass
branches.cn: 浏览器把同一个旧词显示在玻璃屏上

branches.en: a thumb moving quickly along the edge of a magazine
branches.cn: 拇指沿着杂志边缘快速翻动

branches.en: a voice repeating a name through a ceiling speaker
branches.cn: 声音通过天花板上的喇叭重复一个名字

branches.en: a paperless notice that still calls itself a page
branches.cn: 一份没有纸的通知仍然自称页面

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin noun pagina and the verb pangere, with English endings that produce a device and a numbering verb.
intro.cn: 这个词依托拉丁名词 pagina 与动词 pangere，再加上英语词尾，生出设备名和表示编号的动词。

latinIntro.en: Pagina, the Latin noun for a column of writing, and pangere, the verb to fasten, stand behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 pagina（书写的一栏）与动词 pangere（固定）是英语这个词背后的来源。

items.meaning: column of writing on a roll
a leaf of a book; a young servant

derivatives.zh: 由 page 加 -er 构成，指寻呼机
由 paginate 加 -ion 构成，指页码编排
由 page 与 turner 复合而成，指让人一口气读完的书

definition_zh: 疼痛；痛苦；辛劳；使痛苦
definition_en: the feeling of physical hurt, deep emotional suffering, or the effort and trouble that something costs
core_image: 一只手按住肋侧，眉头因为一阵刺痛而皱起
scene: 雨夜里，老人扶着墙慢慢坐下，手掌一直按着膝盖。The pain in his knee kept him awake until dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 pain 是「身体的疼痛」（第 1 个义项：生理上的痛感）；句意是膝盖的疼痛让他一直醒到天亮。图中可辨识的物件：夜雨、墙、老人按住膝盖的手。

collocations.zh: 成长中的烦恼；发展初期的阵痛

derivatives.zh: 由 pain 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「令人疼痛的；痛苦的」
由 pain 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「无痛的」
由 pain 与 killer 复合而成，义为「止痛药」
由 pain 加 -ed 构成，义为「显出痛苦的」

senses.title: Physical hurt in the body
senses.definition: an unpleasant feeling in the body caused by injury or illness
senses.definitionCN: 由受伤或疾病引起的身体上的不适感觉
senses.example: The pain in his knee kept him awake until dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 膝盖的疼痛让他一直醒到天亮。
senses.why: Latin poena meant a penalty, so the word starts from something imposed on a person rather than chosen; bodily hurt is felt as a price.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 poena 意为「惩罚」，所以这个词的起点是加在人身上的东西，而不是自己挑的；身体的痛就像被收走的一笔代价。

senses.title: Deep emotional suffering
senses.definition: a feeling of great sadness or distress that is not caused by physical injury
senses.definitionCN: 并非由身体损伤引起、而是源于内心的巨大悲伤或难受
senses.example: The pain of losing her friend never fully left her.
senses.exampleCN: 失去朋友的痛苦始终没有完全离开她。
senses.why: If pain is a penalty paid, it can also be paid in the mind, so the same word covers grief that leaves no visible wound.
senses.whyCN: 既然 pain 是一笔要付的代价，也就可以在心里付；于是同一个词也覆盖了看不见伤口的悲伤。

senses.title: Effort and trouble taken
senses.definition: the effort and careful work that someone puts into doing something properly, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 为把事情做好而付出的努力与细心，通常用复数
senses.example: She took great pains to hide the crack in the vase.
senses.exampleCN: 她费了好大功夫才把花瓶上的裂缝藏住。
senses.why: Anything worth doing exactly right costs some discomfort, so the plural pains came to mean the trouble one is willing to spend.
senses.whyCN: 凡是要做到位的事都得付点不舒服的代价，于是复数 pains 转而指人愿意花出去的那份心力。

senses.title: To cause someone hurt or distress
senses.definition: to make someone feel physical or emotional hurt
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到身体上或情绪上的难受
senses.example: It pained him to admit that he had been wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 承认自己错了让他很难受。
senses.why: The noun became a verb by reversing the direction: instead of feeling the penalty, a person or event now imposes it on someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词时方向反了过来：不再是承受那份惩罚，而是某人或某事把它加到别人身上。

intro.en: Pain goes back to a Latin word for penalty, which reached English through French and slowly moved from punishment to the hurt a body or mind feels.
intro.cn: pain 可追到拉丁语中表示「惩罚」的词，经法语进入英语，词义从处罚慢慢移到身体或心里感到的痛。

items.en: Poena meant penalty, punishment, or the price paid for a wrong.
items.cn: poena 意为处罚、惩罚，或为过错付出的代价。

items.en: The adjective poenalis described what belongs to punishment, and it survives in English penal.
items.cn: 形容词 poenalis 描述与惩罚有关的东西，在英语中留下 penal 一词。

items.en: Old French peine took over the sense of punishment and also of hardship and suffering.
items.cn: 古法语 peine 承接了「惩罚」，也带上「艰苦、受苦」的意思。

items.en: Middle English pain named both the penalty and the bodily hurt, and the bodily sense gradually became the main one.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pain 既指惩罚也指身体的伤痛，后来身体上的痛感渐渐成了主要意思。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical sense, adds the emotional one, and keeps the plural as a word for effort.
items.cn: 现代英语保留身体痛感，添上情绪上的痛苦，并让复数形式表示付出的辛劳。

note.en: The look-alike group collects legal relatives of the Latin word for penalty; the near-meaning group collects words for hurt and suffering.
note.cn: 形近组收源自「惩罚」这一拉丁词的司法同族词；近义组收表示伤痛与受苦的词。

entries.definition: The Latin noun for penalty, the source of the English word.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示惩罚的名词，是英语这个词的来源。

entries.definition: Relating to punishment by law.
entries.definitionCN: 与法律上的惩罚有关的。

entries.definition: A punishment for breaking a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 因违反规则而受到的处罚。

entries.definition: To long for something sadly; it is only close in spelling, and its source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 苦苦思念；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A continuous dull pain.
entries.definitionCN: 持续而隐约的疼痛。

entries.definition: The state of being tender and painful to touch.
entries.definitionCN: 一碰就疼的状态。

entries.definition: Serious pain of body or mind that lasts.
entries.definitionCN: 持续的身体或精神痛苦。

entries.definition: Extreme worry, sadness or discomfort.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的忧虑、悲伤或不适。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin noun for penalty, and its family runs from legal punishment to bodily hurt and the effort people spend.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「惩罚」的拉丁名词上，同族词从法律处罚一路延伸到身体的痛和人们肯花的力气。

normal.en: Latin poena is a penalty, so pain is something charged to you rather than something you choose.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 poena 是惩罚，所以 pain 是被记在你账上的东西，而不是你自己挑的。

normal.en: Penal and penalty keep the legal side of poena visible in modern English.
normal.cn: penal 和 penalty 让 poena 的司法一面在现代英语里仍然看得见。

normal.en: The suffix -ful in painful adds fullness: a thing that is full of pain.
normal.cn: painful 里的后缀 -ful 添上「满」的意思：一件装满疼痛的东西。

normal.en: The suffix -less in painless removes it: a state with no pain at all.
normal.cn: painless 里的后缀 -less 把它去掉：完全没有疼痛的状态。

normal.en: Take pains is the old idea of paying a price, now spent as careful effort.
normal.cn: take pains 原本是「付出代价」的老想法，如今花出去的是细致的用心。

abstract.en: A word that once meant a fine now means a hurt, which suggests we treat pain as something the body pays.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经表示罚款的词如今表示疼痛，说明我们把痛当成身体付出的东西。

abstract.en: Pain is the body's way of charging attention to a place that needs care.
abstract.cn: 疼痛是身体把注意力记到某个需要照料的地方。

abstract.en: The plural pains reminds us that careful work also has a cost, just a quieter one.
abstract.cn: 复数 pains 提醒人：细心的活儿也有代价，只是安静一些。

examples.en: The pain in his knee kept him awake until dawn.
examples.cn: 膝盖的疼痛让他一直醒到天亮。

examples.en: The pain of losing her friend never fully left her.
examples.cn: 失去朋友的痛苦始终没有完全离开她。

examples.en: It pained him to admit that he had been wrong.
examples.cn: 承认自己错了让他很难受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佩恩」——佩恩磕到桌角，疼得直吸凉气；pain 就是疼痛。

root: 拉丁语 poena（惩罚、代价）经古法语 peine 进入英语；一般认为词义由「受罚」转到「受苦、疼痛」，同族词多与处罚、痛感有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a hurt that costs you something; the senses divide into bodily pain, grief of the mind, the effort one pays out, and the act of hurting someone.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一种要你付出代价的痛；义项分为身体的痛、心里的苦、肯付出去的辛劳，以及让别人难受的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressed to the ribs while a sharp ache narrows the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按住肋侧，一阵刺痛让眉头皱起。

branches.en: a hand pressed hard against a sore knee
branches.cn: 一只手紧紧按住发疼的膝盖

branches.en: an empty chair that still hurts to look at
branches.cn: 一把看一眼就难受的空椅子

branches.en: a careful hand hiding a crack in a vase
branches.cn: 一只手小心地把花瓶裂缝遮住

branches.en: a face that has just heard its own mistake named
branches.cn: 刚听到自己错误被点破的一张脸

branches.en: one word holding a wound and a grief together
branches.cn: 同一个词同时装着伤口和悲伤

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin noun of penalty, its adjective, and two English suffixes that add or remove pain.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示惩罚的拉丁名词、它的形容词，以及两个给「痛」添上或去掉的后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Poena, the Latin noun for penalty, and its adjective poenalis stand behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 poena（惩罚）及其形容词 poenalis 是英语这个词背后的来源。

derivatives.zh: 由 pain 加 -ful 构成，指令人疼痛的
由 pain 加 -less 构成，指无痛的
由 pain 与 killer 复合而成，指止痛药
